headline: Meta has released free code so that people can build their own gadgets that run its new AI assistant, Muse.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a real product step that opens Muse to builders, though small in scale (5,000 devices) and clearly a hobby project.
importance_line: Hobbyists and developers get a free way to put Meta's AI assistant into homemade devices, but Meta says it made just 5,000 of its own home-control box and itself warns builders to proceed at their own risk.
summary: The Verge reports that Meta has opened up the code for its new AI assistant, Muse, so people can connect it to their own screens, buttons and sensors, for example a small display that shows reminders. Meta is also giving away a home-control box called Muse Home Link, with a waiting list open and shipping due sometime this month, and Meta executive Nat Friedman says 5,000 were made.
notes: Announcement date not stated in the article; published 2 Oct 2026, treated as new today.
